items.body:

scenario.title: Complete Power Outage at HQ
scenario.kicker: Business Continuity Tabletop · ISO/IEC 27001:2022 & ISO/IEC 27002:2022 · Business Operations · Advanced · 90 minutes · Facilitated discussion

rules: Tabletop Exercises are NOT “Pass” or “Fail” activities.
Treat the exercise scenarios as real events and assume that normal operational procedures and resources are in place.
There is no need to name specific cybersecurity technologies — focus on the processes for incident response.
All participants are encouraged to actively engage and contribute to discussions.
Approach the scenarios with a problem-solving mindset.
You are encouraged to highlight areas for improvement and suggest practical enhancements.
Actively participate in the evaluation process at the end of the exercise to identify “Lessons Learned”.

objectives.title: Objectives & ground rules
items: Test decision-making when customer care continuity is at stake
Map every decision to ISO/IEC 27001:2022 continuity and operational controls
Expose gaps in care capacity, customer communication and recovery
Leave with an after-action list with owners and dates

data.ground_rules: Stay in role. No wrong answers — this is a discussion, not a test. Call out what you don't know. Every decision gets an Annex A control.

slides.name: After Action Executive Summary

data.participants: Operations Director, Customer Care Managers, Team Leaders, Client Delivery, Workforce Management
highlights: Triage was completed before the floor went dark, protecting in-flight customer interactions
Emergency and complaint lines continued through the fallback arrangement
The client knew the revised timeline before the SLA was breached
lessons: The inbound care program's dependency on HQ needs a documented contingency
Fallback work arrangements must be tested at real care scale
Release-or-hold decisions for the floor need a pre-agreed script
data.story: Weekday 15:00, with the client's billing-cycle announcement driving peak inbound call volumes into the close of day. The exercise unfolded through the following injects: At 15:05, Regional power loss — A regional outage hits HQ; the UPS carries the floor briefly but the backup generators fail to start. At 15:20, Floor shutting down — Workstations and telephony shut down mid-call; inbound customers are disconnected and 100% of care agents are losing their systems. At 16:00, Extended outage confirmed — The utility reports power out for 25% of the operating day or more; generators can be repaired, but not before midnight. The inbound care SLA is at risk. The hotwash closed on a single question: Would our inbound customer care service have survived an outage lasting 25% of the operating day? Where does the inbound answer-time SLA break first? Every decision was mapped to an ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A control, and the exercise ended with a set of owned follow-up actions.

data.executive_assessment: The team should complete scoring from the exercise transcript. Expected strengths to verify: customer communication, care-queue prioritisation and team coordination. Expected gaps to verify: minimum-viable-staffing decisions, unanswered-call and backlog recovery speed, alternate care arrangements, SLA/credit handling and audit-ready continuity documentation.

framework_alignment.theme: Care continuity governance, roles, escalation, customer communication
Care workforce availability, scheduling, attendance and wellbeing
Care capacity: inbound answer times, queue prioritisation, unanswered-call backlog recovery

kpis.kpi: Time to activate the continuity plan after a care-service disruption
Priority care queues kept live (emergency and complaint lines)
Calls answered within the agreed service level during the disruption
Unanswered inbound calls cleared from the disruption backlog
Customer notifications issued within the agreed window
Staffing coverage against minimum viable care staffing
Customer SLA adherence during and after the disruption
Service credits paid vs SLA exposure

decisions: Approve a funded continuity programme covering alternate care-delivery arrangements, staffing capacity and remote-work readiness for the customer care operation.
Designate a single executive owner for customer-care continuity CAPA governance and monthly reporting until all high-priority items are closed and validated.
Direct Care Operations, Workforce Management, HR and Client Delivery to finalise minimum-viable-staffing and customer-notification matrices within 30 days.
Require a follow-up customer-care continuity tabletop within 180 days using the same scoring model and evidence-pack requirements.
evidence: Care continuity plan versions, trigger records and the time-stamped decision log.
Customer notification log: who was told, when, by whom and against which SLA clause.
Care workforce evidence: attendance records, rosters, redeployment decisions and shift changes.
Care capacity evidence: inbound call and chat volumes, answer times, abandonment and unanswered-call backlog tracking.
Continuity-drill records: alternate care arrangements, remote work, results and gaps.
Recovery and improvement evidence: SLA reconciliation, customer reporting, RCA, CAPA closure and management review.

roadmap.milestones: Assign care continuity owners; publish the customer-notification matrix; define minimum viable staffing per care queue; confirm alternate care arrangements and remote capacity.
Run care continuity and remote-work drills; test inbound backlog-recovery playbooks; cross-train teams on priority inbound queues; agree SLA relief protocols with key clients.
Run the follow-up customer-care continuity tabletop; close CAPA evidence; embed continuity tests in the operating rhythm; update control narratives and evidence repository.
